Extract coefficients from a fitted cv.rbridge object

Source: R/methods.R
coef.cv.rbridge.Rd

Extract original-scale intercept and slope coefficients from a fitted cross-validated cv.rbridge object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cv.rbridge'
coef(object, s = c("lambda.1se", "lambda.min"), ...)

Arguments

object

Fitted object returned by cv.rbridge, with p predictors in its training design.

s

Penalty selection, using numeric fitted values or a character name. Numeric values must match object$lambda exactly; no interpolation is used. The character selectors are:

"lambda.min"

Select the penalty with minimum CV error.

"lambda.1se"

Select using the historical CV error bars.

The default is lambda.1se.

...

Additional arguments accepted for compatibility.

Value

Numeric matrix with p + 1 rows and one column per selected penalty, even when only one penalty is selected. The first row is (Intercept); subsequent rows are original-scale slopes in the training predictor order.

Details

The returned matrix retains its dimensions for a single selected penalty. The defaults differ between coef() and predict(): coefficient extraction uses lambda.1se, whereas response prediction uses lambda.min. Specify the same s in both calls when comparing coefficients and their predictions. Returned slopes are on the original predictor scale; the linear restrictions concern standardized slopes. See rbridge for converting scales before checking restriction residuals.

See also

predict.cv.rbridge, cv.rbridge

Author

Bahadir Yuzbasi
Maintainer: Bahadir Yuzbasi b.yzb@hotmail.com

Examples

# Reproducible synthetic demonstration: 100 observations, eight predictors.
set.seed(2019)
beta <- c(3, 1.5, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0)
p <- length(beta)
beta <- matrix(beta, nrow = p, ncol = 1)
n <- 100
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta + rnorm(n))
# A user-specified sum of standardized slopes: b[1] + b[2] + b[5] = 6.5.
# This target is illustrative; it is not asserted to equal the generating sum.
R1.mat <- matrix(c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 1)
r1.vec <- matrix(6.5, nrow = 1, ncol = 1)

# Five penalties keep this help example fast; the default is 100.
model1 <- cv.rbridge(X, y, q = 1, R = R1.mat, r = r1.vec, nlambda = 5,
                     nfolds = 3, num_threads = 1)
# A single selected penalty still gives a coefficient matrix.
coefficients <- coef(model1, s = "lambda.min")
coefficients
#>             802.149726533951
#> (Intercept)       0.01283347
#> V1                2.98320054
#> V2                1.57870923
#> V3                0.00000000
#> V4                0.00000000
#> V5                1.99412306
#> V6                0.00000000
#> V7                0.00000000
#> V8                0.00000000
dim(coefficients)
#> [1] 9 1
# The default uses the historical error-bar selector.
coef(model1)
#>             802.149726533951
#> (Intercept)       0.01283347
#> V1                2.98320054
#> V2                1.57870923
#> V3                0.00000000
#> V4                0.00000000
#> V5                1.99412306
#> V6                0.00000000
#> V7                0.00000000
#> V8                0.00000000
